title: 4 Ways Nordic Retailers and Suppliers can Compete with Global Marketplaces
summary: Learn how to compete with global marketplaces without racing on price. Four Nordic retailer strengths, backed by 2026 data, and how SPS Commerce supports each.
body_markdown:
How can Nordic retailers compete with Temu and Shein? Not by matching their prices.


In 2026 the picture has shifted. A new EU customs fee has dampened low-value parcel imports, regulators are scrutinizing product safety on global marketplaces, and Nordic shoppers still value what local retailers do best.


This blog looks at four strengths that Nordic retailers and suppliers hold over global marketplaces. Price is where marketplaces are strongest. Trust, reliable delivery, fast supplier onboarding and compliance are where Nordic businesses can win, and all four depend on a well-connected retail supply chain.


## Has the picture shifted for Nordic retailers in 2026?


Yes, partly. Since 1 July, the EU charges a flat €3 customs duty on parcels worth €150 or less that arrive from outside the bloc. In Sweden,[the share of consumers who bought from Temu or Shein fell to 8% in July 2026, from 18% in July 2025](https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4511526/proppen-ur-for-e-handeln?lang=sv) , according to Svensk Handel’s E-handelsindikator report of 25 August 2026. In May, the European Commission also[fined Temu €200 million](https://wtop.com/europe/2026/05/chinese-online-retailer-temu-hit-with-232-million-fine-over-illegal-products/) for failing to assess the risk of illegal products on its marketplace.


Two cautions apply.[Svensk Handel says it is too early to call the drop permanent](https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4511526/proppen-ur-for-e-handeln?lang=sv) , because these companies are working to build the fee into checkout. And Shein held up better than Temu,[helped by a planned warehouse inside the EU](https://www.euronews.com/2026/08/27/eu-tax-chinese-small-parcels-plunge-30-to-40) .


The picture also differs by country.[PostNord’s Spring 2026 survey of 4,000 consumers](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) ranks the most common marketplaces in each market:

Norway is outside the EU, so the duty does not apply there. Its government has[proposed cutting the clothing tariff to 5% in the 2027 budget](https://www.frifagbevegelse.no/hknytt/skuffet-over-temu-grep-darlig-for-norske-arbeidsplasser/2720582) , while online goods under NOK 3,000 still enter duty-free. The window is open, but it is not guaranteed. What retailers do with it matters more than the policy.


Against this backdrop, Nordic retailers and suppliers hold **four strengths** that are hard for global marketplaces to replicate. Below, each one is set out with the evidence behind it and where retail and supplier network solutions can help.


## 1) Local trust and choice


#### How can Nordic retailers compete with global marketplaces beyond price?


By winning on what shoppers value beyond the lowest price: choice, clear returns, a smooth checkout and a brand they trust.[PostNord’s 2026 survey shows these matter](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) . In Sweden, Denmark and Finland, being able to choose a pickup location is the top factor when deciding where to shop (82%, 78% and 84%). In each country, between 68% and 72% of consumers say a clear return policy is important. Norway is the exception: lowest price ranks first there, at 78%.


Local retailers also have home ground. In Finland,[eight of the ten most visited online stores are Finnish, and purchases from Finnish online stores grew slightly faster than purchases from abroad in 2025.](https://kauppa.fi/en/uutishuone/2026/03/23/recent-finnish-commerce-federation-survey-domestic-e-commerce-grew-by-5-3-per-cent-in-2025-social-media-still-guides-the-purchasing-behaviour-of-older-age-groups/) PostNord suggests that[Norwegians’ shift toward Swedish and Danish shops](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) may reflect a preference for closer, more reliable markets with faster deliveries, easier returns and higher trust.


Each of these strengths is a promise made at the front end. Keeping it depends on the back end: whether suppliers ship what was ordered, when it was ordered. This is where retail and supplier network solutions such as[SPS Commerce](https://www.spscommerce.com/) help. They connect retailers and suppliers on one network, so orders, shipping notices and invoices move between partners without manual rework. The SPS network spans more than 300,000 trading relationships. Orchestrate adds shared context across companies, so when something goes wrong, the right person knows early.


## 2) Reliable delivery


#### How does reliable delivery help retailers compete with global marketplaces?


By making a delivery promise the retailer can keep. Amazon and Zalando have shaped what shoppers expect.[PostNord notes that younger consumers favor them](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) because fast delivery, reviews and loyalty programs support habitual shopping. Amazon still ranks first among marketplaces in Sweden, at 33%, although it has lost ground in Denmark, Finland and Norway.


Delivery terms decide sales. In Norway,[6 in 10 consumers cancelled a purchase at checkout in the past three months, up from 5 in 10](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) , most often because shipping was too expensive. In Finland,[one in five has paid for same-day delivery, and twice as many say they would](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) .


A reliable delivery promise starts upstream in the retail supply chain. Stock levels, shipping notices and supplier lead times have to be accurate before a shopper sees “in stock.” Marketplace technology provider Mirakl[reports that site availability in H&M’s dropship program rose from 80% to 99.78%](https://www.mirakl.com/blogs/marketplace/how-marketplace-and-dropship-are-reshaping-ecommerce-across-the-nordic-region/) .


Proper retail and supplier network solutions can help retailers see where orders stand across suppliers, and which suppliers cause the gaps.[SPS Visibility Management](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/visibility-management/) , for example, shows every active purchase order across the teams that depend on it, and[SPS Performance Management](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/performance-management/) benchmarks supplier scorecards against the network. A 2025[Forrester Total Economic Impact study](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/tei-of-performance-suite/) of SPS found a 5% reduction in stockouts and 42% less effort in receiving.


## 3) Fast supplier onboarding


#### How can retailers match marketplace speed in supplier onboarding?


By onboarding suppliers on a network that already knows the requirements, instead of building each connection from scratch. Marketplaces grow their range by adding sellers quickly. Elkjøp, the Nordic electronics retailer, has[scaled its marketplace to about 240 sellers and 200,000 offers across four Nordic markets](https://www.mirakl.com/blogs/marketplace/how-marketplace-and-dropship-are-reshaping-ecommerce-across-the-nordic-region/) . Retailers that want a wider range need supplier onboarding that keeps pace.


Nordic suppliers show what readiness looks like. Vitamin Well, the Stockholm-founded group behind Barebells and NOCCO, started with one operations specialist processing every order, shipping notice and invoice by hand. When a US retailer required EDI, the team had no experience with it. With[SPS Fulfillment](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/fulfillment/edi/) feeding its ERP system, Vitamin Well has[onboarded more than 100 trading partners and grown from about 1,000 trading documents a month in January 2024 to more than 5,000](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/vitamin-well-case-study/) . Its supply planning manager estimates that manual work and errors fell by more than 95%, and says the team of five would otherwise need to be at least twice the size. “It eliminates the risk for human error,” he says.


Smaller partners that do not use EDI can still join the same automated workflow through[PDF Order Automation](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/pdf-order-automation/) . Most of Vitamin Well’s retail customers recommended SPS themselves, so the systems and onboarding steps were already mapped.


The lesson works in both directions. Retailers that are easy to trade with reach growing brands faster, and suppliers that are automated can say yes to more retailers. Solutions such as SPS Commerce support both sides.[SPS Relationship Management](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/relationship-management/) , for example, gets every supplier ready before the first order ships and keeps them aligned as requirements change.


## 4) Product compliance


#### Why is product compliance a competitive advantage?


Because trust is hard to copy, and compliance is how Nordic retailers earn it.[PostNord notes that Nordic retailers typically operate under stricter rules on consumer protection, product standards and sustainability](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) , which makes competing on price alone difficult. The same rules can work in their favor as regulators look harder at global marketplaces.


In May, the European Commission[fined Temu €200 million for failing to properly assess the risk of illegal products on its marketplace](https://wtop.com/europe/2026/05/chinese-online-retailer-temu-hit-with-232-million-fine-over-illegal-products/) , citing items such as baby toys and small electronics that did not meet EU safety rules. Separately,[a 2025 EU survey found that more than 60% of low-value products inspected did not meet European requirements or safety standards](https://www.euronews.com/2026/08/27/eu-tax-chinese-small-parcels-plunge-30-to-40) .


For retailers, this turns compliance from a cost into a message: these products come from suppliers we know, with documentation we can show. Making that message true takes organized product and partner data. A good retail and supplier network solution can support compliance between trading partners. When a retailer’s requirements change, the network detects the change, updates it and applies it once for everyone, so suppliers are not chasing rules one retailer at a time.[SPS Assortment](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/assortment/) , for instance, helps keep product information complete and accurate across channels. Product safety testing itself stays with manufacturers and certifiers.


## What should Nordic retailers do next to compete with Temu and Shein?


Use the window to strengthen what marketplaces cannot easily copy. Start with four checks:


- **Trust:** Which strengths do your shoppers value beyond price, such as pickup choice and clear returns, and does your supply chain support them?


- **Delivery:** Can you see every open purchase order, and which suppliers put your availability at risk?


- **Onboarding:** How long does it take to get a new supplier or brand live?


- **Compliance:** Can you show where a product came from and which requirements it meets?


Price pressure will not disappear. The customs fee is temporary, and the companies behind it are adapting. A supply chain that keeps its promises is a lasting advantage. ## Frequently asked questions


#### Is the EU customs fee working?


Early data say yes.[Small-parcel imports into the EU are down 30% to 40% since 1 July](https://www.euronews.com/2026/08/27/eu-tax-chinese-small-parcels-plunge-30-to-40) , and[the share of Swedish consumers buying from Temu or Shein fell from 18% in July 2025 to 8% in July 2026](https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4511526/proppen-ur-for-e-handeln?lang=sv) , according to Svensk Handel’s report of 25 August 2026. Svensk Handel says it is too early to call this permanent, and the duty is a temporary measure meant to bridge to a broader customs reform in 2028.


#### Can Nordic retailers beat Temu on price?


Rarely, and they do not need to.[PostNord links Temu’s rise to price sensitivity](https://www.postnord.com/siteassets/PDF/PN_E-commerce_Spring_2026.pdf) , while Nordic retailers operate under stricter rules on consumer protection and product standards. Their edge lies in choice, returns, trust and reliable delivery.


#### How can suppliers onboard with new retailers faster?


By automating orders, shipping notices and invoices instead of handling them by hand, and by using a network where retailer requirements are already mapped.[Vitamin Well onboarded more than 100 trading partners this way](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/vitamin-well-case-study/) .


#### How can network solutions such as SPS Commerce help retailers facing global marketplaces?


Retail and supplier network solutions such as SPS connect retailers and suppliers on one network. They help with supplier onboarding, order visibility, supplier performance and compliance between trading partners. They do not change shopper-facing prices or the online storefront.
